thread:
Emily (Marketing): hey @Sam @Jordan — planning the webinar demo for next Wed. marketing needs benchmark artifacts + a short methodology blurb to back any latency/cost claims. can you help with a reproducible data pack (raw CSVs + summary) by Mon EOD?

Emily (Marketing): specific asks: 1) raw per-run CSV with p50/p95/p99 + token-level breakdown 2) variant comparison: redwood-1.3b fp16 vs quantized q4f 3) two seq lengths: ~2048 (chat) and ~8192 (long) 4) both backend-only and end-to-end (api+proxy) numbers 5) 100 sample prompts used (attach) + exact warmup steps + run command to reproduce 6) note on any tuning (batching, kv-cache priming)

Sam (Eng Runtime): ack — can do. quick clarifying q's: which regions? and do you want embedding latencies too?

Emily (Marketing): regions: us-west-2 and eu-west-1. embeddings not needed for the launch claims, only text generation.

Jordan (Eng Runtime): we can run a smoke pass today and full sweep Thu. decide whether "end-to-end" should include client-side serialization. recommend two flavors: backend-only (runtime container) and observed-api (our gateway+network). which do you prefer for the headline?

Carlos (Marketing): for headlines, prefer backend-only for raw engine claims, but we need observed-api for customer-facing numbers. also flag cold-starts. don’t put p99 in a headline unless it's rock solid. :thumbsup:

Priya (Data Ops): for CSV reproducibility we'll output schema like: run_id,model,variant,seq_len,prompt_tokens,generated_tokens,total_tokens,latency_ms,backend_latency_ms,kernel_ms,region,timestamp,run_notes. we can also include a small JSON per-run with flags (warmup=true/false, batch_size). want that?

Emily (Marketing): yes to both CSV + per-run JSON metadata. also include the exact git sha for the runtime image and model artifact IDs. link to sample prompts: https://drive.google.com/drive/fake-link/webinar-samples (attached).

Sam (Eng Runtime): cool. reproducer (internal bench runner) — will run like this:

```bash
# example repro command (internal)
bench-run 
  --model redwood-1.3b 
  --variant q4f,fp16 
  --prompts ./samples/webinar-100.txt 
  --seq-lens 2048,8192 
  --region us-west-2,eu-west-1 
  --runs-per-config 50 
  --output ./artifacts/webinar_bench_$(date +%s).csv
  --emit-json-metadata ./artifacts/webinar_meta_$(date +%s).json

# note: we'll run once cold (no warmup) and once with KV warmup loop = 10 iterations
```

Sam (Eng Runtime): timeline: smoke today (backend-only, single region), full sweep Thu (both regions + end-to-end). will upload artifacts to internal GCS path and post link here when done.

benchbot: run started: webinar-smoke-1755001234 — backend-only us-west-2 (50 runs) — https://ci.internal/runs/1755001234

Jordan (Eng Runtime): small caveat on quant: q4f numbers vary by prompt token distribution. we'll include per-slice breakdown by prompt length bucket and a note that quantized kernel prefers shorter context for best p95.

Priya (Data Ops): we'll produce summary slides with percentiles and heatmaps (cold vs warmed) and a CSV of the 100 sample prompts with their token counts. also will seed a reproducibility script that replays prompts at the same timing.

Carlos (Marketing): awesome. can you flag any runs where variance > 30% p95->p99? we'll avoid using those slices in the webinar slides.

Sam (Eng Runtime): will do. we'll also attach the exact warmup snippet we run (priming the KV cache with the first 10 prompts).

benchbot: run complete: webinar-smoke-1755001234 — artifacts: gs://redwood-internal/bench/webinar-smoke-1755001234.tar.gz

Emily (Marketing): perfect — thanks everyone. please ping if anything blocks the Thu sweep. we need the final artifact link + 1-paragraph methodology by Mon EOD so the content team can write copy. :pray:
